solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Full ticket price shown in street

parts.note: full, as in a full or complete job, means thorough
the price of a ticket for a journey is the fare

explanation.surface: A passenger complains that the full price of a ticket is displayed on the street.
explanation.definitionFit: A busy public road or main route through a town is a synonym for a street.

parts.note: fine, as in a fine thread, means thin

explanation.surface: Someone asked about an item replies that it is fine and good.
explanation.definitionFit: Any unnamed item or article can be called by this vague general word, a synonym for an object.

parts.note: concerning, as in a row over money, can mean over
vision, the faculty of seeing, is sight

explanation.surface: An optician admits an honest error about a patient's eyesight.
explanation.definitionFit: An unintentional slip or failure to notice something is an innocent error of this kind.

clue.text: A bit rusty, like a retired GP?

definitions.meaning: describes skills that have slipped through lack of use
a GP (general practitioner, a family doctor) who has retired no longer runs a medical practice

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a doctor who has stopped working would have lost their touch.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading takes 'practice' as a doctor's surgery: a retired GP is literally no longer in one.
explanation.definitionFit: Being rusty means having lost skill through lack of regular use, the idiom's ordinary sense.

clue.text: Cake and a drink in heart of Burgundy

indicators.note: in tells us the first pieces go inside the letters taken from Burgundy
the heart of a word is its middle, here the two central letters of Burgundy

parts.note: tea is a common drink

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys a slice of cake and a drink in the middle of Burgundy, the French wine region.
explanation.walkthrough: Burgundy has eight letters, so its 'heart' is the central pair rather than a single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A rich, often cream-filled cake takes its name from the French word for cake.

clue.text: Batteries not included in preparing this food

definitions.text: Batteries not included in preparing this food

parts.words: Batteries not included in preparing this food
parts.note: battery farming keeps hens in cages, so food from hens not kept in batteries comes from birds allowed outdoors

explanation.surface: It reads like the small print on a toy box: batteries are not included.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Batteries not included' is the stock warning on gadgets, but here batteries are the cages of intensive poultry farms.
explanation.definitionFit: These come from hens that roam outdoors rather than being kept in battery cages, so no batteries are involved.

indicators.note: coming from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses as nonsense something a brother-in-law said.
explanation.definitionFit: Talking rubbish or drivel is a common informal synonym for nonsense.

clue.text: Strict member of the clergy turned up in diocese

indicators.note: in places the turned clergy title inside the word for a diocese

parts.note: a bishop's see is the diocese he or she oversees

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is the title of a member of the clergy

explanation.surface: A stern clergyman makes an appearance in his diocese.
explanation.definitionFit: Harsh, stern and uncompromising, as a strict teacher or a severe punishment is.

indicators.note: in places the reflected writer inside the word it
reflected, as in a mirror, means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a pen is a writing implement, a writer

explanation.surface: An author is embarrassed to see themselves mirrored in a piece of work.
explanation.definitionFit: Clumsy or lacking skill, as an awkward attempt is, is a synonym for the answer.

indicators.note: involving means the rearranged letters surround the abbreviation for English
new suggests a fresh arrangement of the letters of threat

explanation.surface: A fresh danger has arisen involving an English playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New' makes THATRE from THREAT, and 'involving' puts E inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A playhouse is a building where plays are staged, an older synonym for this venue.

clue.text: Reversal of decline in fossil fuel

indicators.note: reversal of says the word for decline is read backwards

parts.note: to sag is to droop or decline

explanation.surface: A trend in the energy market: the fall in fossil fuel use has turned around.
explanation.definitionFit: Natural gas is a fossil fuel formed from ancient organic matter, an example of the category.

indicators.note: importing means taking something in, so the country surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: France is a country

explanation.surface: A trade story: one country brings in a perfume made in Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasant smell or perfume is a scent, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Working in a centre for fruit

indicators.note: working suggests the letters are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone employed in a fruit distribution centre.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth-skinned variety of peach is an example of fruit.

clue.text: Fury as old car fails to start

indicators.note: fails to start says the first letter is dropped, as a car that will not start

parts.note: a banger is British slang for an old, battered car

explanation.surface: A driver is furious when their old car won't start.
explanation.walkthrough: A banger is British slang for a ramshackle old car; 'fails to start' drops its first letter, B.
explanation.definitionFit: Fury is extreme rage, so the two are synonyms of differing intensity.

indicators.note: casing means enclosing, so the word for quickly surrounds the letter for hotel

parts.note: apace means quickly
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A Native American swiftly scouts out a hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: These are a group of Native American peoples of the American Southwest, an example of the definition.

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation for hot inside the word for pleasant

parts.note: nice means pleasant
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: Someone finds a warm, pleasant corner to sit in.
explanation.definitionFit: A recess or nook, or figuratively a specialised corner of a market, fits the definition.

parts.note: an ear is the organ that listens

explanation.surface: Someone flatly refuses to give the name of the person who overheard.
explanation.definitionFit: This informal British exclamation is an emphatic refusal, meaning definitely not.

clue.text: All right to be carried by the man on lorry leaving plant

indicators.note: on means the following piece comes after the word for lorry

parts.note: an artic is an articulated lorry, a British term for a large truck

indicators.note: carried by means held inside the pronoun for the man

parts.note: he is the pronoun for the man
OK means all right

explanation.surface: A man rides on a departing lorry carrying something all right.
explanation.walkthrough: An artic is British for an articulated lorry, a large truck; 'leaving' simply links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The globe and Jerusalem kinds are thistle-like vegetables, examples of a plant.

explanation.surface: Someone resolves to take legal steps in court.
explanation.definitionFit: To take steps is to do something or take action, a synonym phrase.

definitions.meaning: taking what is not yours means stealing
a crime such as stealing is an offence

explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking offence' reads as a phrase for feeling insulted, but the two words are separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealing is both a taking of property and a criminal offence.

parts.note: the height of fashion means the latest style, but here height means how high a skirt's bottom edge sits

explanation.surface: It reads as praise for the latest look in women's clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The bottom edge of a skirt or dress sets how high it reaches, and fashions in it rise and fall.

definitions.meaning: as in ... and wife, a husband
a bishop is one of the pieces in chess

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a husband might be a bishop.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess sense is the twist: pieces are called men, and a bishop is one.
explanation.definitionFit: Husband and male partner are the same in the phrase man and wife; a chess piece is also called one.

clue.text: Ingrained dirt, dreadful by end of aisle

indicators.note: by means the next piece sits beside the word for dreadful

parts.note: grim means dreadful

indicators.note: end of takes the last letter of aisle

explanation.surface: A cleaner finds terrible, ingrained dirt at the end of a supermarket aisle.
explanation.definitionFit: Soot or dirt worked deep into a surface is a precise synonym for ingrained dirt.

indicators.note: faulty suggests the letters of the word are out of order and need rearranging

explanation.surface: An air force officer concludes, looking back, that the interceptor jets were defective.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking back on past events is what both phrases describe, so they are synonymous.
